title: Adaptive telemetry sampling and cost-aware SLIs for console analytics ingest
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Our analytics ingest pipeline is producing high-cardinality telemetry and tracing volumes that inflate storage and query costs while making SLO signal noisy for low-traffic tenants. This ticket designs and implements an adaptive telemetry strategy that reduces cost, preserves critical SLIs, and ensures traceability from console routes down to downstream aggregations.

Goals:
- Define a minimal, prioritized SLI set for ingest health and query correctness that preserves customer-facing guarantees.
- Implement adaptive sampling rules (by tenant, route, and signal severity) to reduce cost while maintaining statistical validity of SLO windows.
- Add cost-aware retention tiers and automatic downsampling for historical telemetry.
- Ensure trace/span correlation is preserved at sampling boundaries for post-incident investigations.
- Provide Grafana dashboards and runbooks that reflect new sampling/retention behavior and the mapping from sampled telemetry to SLO calculations.

Scope and deliverables:
- SLI/SLO definitions: request ingestion success rate (1m/1h/24h), median/95/99 latency for ingest pipeline, telemetry-to-query latency, and completeness metric for sampled traces.
- Sampling engine: a lightweight policy service that evaluates per-tenant sampling rate based on traffic, recent error rate, and budget. Local deterministic hashing to ensure consistent sampling for related spans/keys.
- Retention policy: hot-tier (30d at full fidelity), warm-tier (90d at reduced cardinality/aggregates), cold-tier (365d aggregates), with automatic promotion/demotion.
- Dashboarding: new panels in the console analytics Observability folder + templated tenant selector; expose sampled vs unsampled comparisons and cost impact by tenant.
- Alerts and runbooks: SLI burn rates and sampling algorithm degradation alerts, with remediation steps.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the ingestion storage backend. We will leverage existing metrics pipeline and implement sampling upstream to reduce volume.
- Full per-tenant bespoke retention contracts (handled later as Dedicated/Private feature).

Success criteria:
- 30–50% reduction in ingest storage cost for analytics telemetry in the pilot tenant group without >5% degradation in SLO accuracy over 7d windows.
- Reduction in query latency for analytics dashboards by 15% on average due to smaller index sizes.
- Clear trace correlation for sampled sessions preserved in >99% of retained traces used for incident debug.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Adaptive+Sampling+Spec
- Initial design mockup (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/file/d/1a2b3c-adaptive-sampling-design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/pull/414
- Grafana dashboard (dev folder): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/console-observability/telemetry-sampling

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Deterministic hashing vs. upstream probabilistic sampling: deterministic ensures related spans are sampled together at the cost of slightly more implementation complexity in the sampler. We chose deterministic for debugability.
- Sampling triggered by both traffic and error-rate to avoid losing rare but important error signals. This increases control-plane churn but reduces unknown blind spots.
- Storage cost vs. SLO faithfulness: we will tune initial thresholds conservatively (lower sampling for low-error tenants) and expand after pilot telemetry analysis.

Integration points and dependencies:
- Ingest router (ENG-19827) for header propagation and sampling hooks.
- Metrics ingestion pipeline (ENG-61234) for downstream retention changes.
- Console dashboard templates (ENG-15344) for new panels.

Customer impact: medium
